intelligence.human_view: Understanding is not the wrapping on the deed — it is the deed. A person who cannot read what they are agreeing to has not agreed to anything, however beautiful the page. That is why the same afternoon produced four different answers to one question: the unfold answers "how do I read it without drowning", the little eyes answer "what does this word mean", the hook answers "why should I care", and the language wiring answers "can I read it in my own words at all". Each one is the same job from a different side. And the failure notes are the same job from the other side: a promise that never settles is a deed that never arrives; a proof with no record is work that never happened; an intake measured as a batch is a verdict that never gets said. The machine's lesson for this group says it plainly: the wiring covers the whole walk including the new end and the agreement — the deed must be understood in their language.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you're an ambassador for your whole school! That doesn't mean you sell things — it means you REPRESENT your school to the world! You're part of it — part of your class, part of your school, part of your whole world! And you tell everybody how wonderful it is, because it's yours!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like mending a dress, love — you must look at the whole dress first, with all its ribbons and buttons, before you start stitching. If you mend from an old pattern that's missing the prettiest part, you'll sew it right out and never notice. Look at the real thing first, keep everything lovely, and then fix what's torn.
intelligence.naya_view: I keep the deed its own step, before the pricing page — never on it. Sign the deed → receive your world → you're hired → pricing page. The deed is the contract: the land, the building, the business, the brand, and your permission to use them — it protects you, and it protects us, because now we both know how it works. Nothing agreement-worded goes on the pricing page itself.
